hook_text: Stop, yield, speed limit. Three road signs, three different shapes, and one of them is not a polygon.
clip_script: Three South African road signs. The stop sign: count the sides, 8, all equal, all corners equal. A regular octagon. The yield sign: 3 equal sides. A regular triangle. The speed sign: run your finger round it. No corners, one curved edge. A circle, and a circle is not a polygon, because polygons have only straight sides. Now the classroom door: 4 sides, 4 square corners, but two sides are longer. A rectangle, which is an irregular quadrilateral. Tilt a square onto its corner and it is still a square. Squash a pentagon and it is still a pentagon. The name comes from counting straight sides. Regular just means all equal. Count the sides, check if they match, and remember the one round shape that stands outside the family.
visual_style: Whiteboard road signs with sides lighting up as they are counted; a square rotating onto its corner and keeping its label; a finger tracing a circle with no corners.
mood: Road trip spotting game, quick and fun.
pacing: Three signs named fast, the door, the tilt and squash tests, then the rule.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and name five shapes you can see from where you are sitting.
